Hi Sara — thank you again for the detailed logs and patience. We’ve completed our internal review and here are the findings and next steps. Attached: redwood_trace_bundle_20280112.tar.gz and proposed-credit-calculation-20280118.xlsx.

Incident summary (Redwood findings):
- Confirmed increased 502/503 responses for requests routed to our us-east-1 shard pool between 2028-01-12T03:01:30Z and 2028-01-12T04:19:10Z (UTC).
- Root cause: a short-lived kernel allocation failure on the serving runtime combined with a subsequent KV-cache eviction storm that amplified tail failures during an autoscaler handoff.
- Impact to CloveCommerce: our telemetry shows a 16.7% reduction in successful checkouts in that window, consistent with your observed ~18% value.

SLA eligibility & compensation:
- Under the terms of your agreement (SLA section 4.2), the incident qualifies for pro-rata service credit. We calculated the credit using the standard formula in Section 5; see the attached spreadsheet for the arithmetic and proposed value.
- Next steps to finalize: please review the proposed credit spreadsheet and reply with any procurement/legal contact for the credit memo. We’ll issue a formal credit note once both legal and finance approve.

Postmortem and remediation:
- We’d like to schedule a joint postmortem on Jan 25, 2028 at 14:00 EST. Agenda: timeline review, log correlation, mitigation actions (kernel allocation patch + autoscaler guardrails), and verification plan.
- Internal remediation already in progress: kernel allocation fix is staged; we’ve added a temporary autoscaler cooldown to reduce handoff amplification.

Attachments referenced in this message: redwood_trace_bundle_20280112.tar.gz (telemetry_summary.csv, shard_eviction.log, kv-cache-evictions.txt), proposed-credit-calculation-20280118.xlsx (credit draft).
